newsitem.title: RUSSIA: MC favours Kondopoga, Syktyvkar in Russia timber.
newsitem.headline: MC favours Kondopoga, Syktyvkar in Russia timber.

text.p: MC Securities, initiating coverage of Russian pulp and paper companies, said in a report it rated Kondopoga and Syktyvkar as its top picks for portfolio investment.
London-based MC also recommended Bratsk Timber at current prices as a long-term play because of its access to cheap timber and proximity to markets in China and India.
In a report issued this month, MC said pulp and paper stocks had been major underperformers in 1996 and were now very cheap.

"An abundance of natural resources, international cost competitiveness and increased domestic consumption will transform this underdeveloped sector into a leading growth industry in Russia over the long run," MC said.
However, it also cautioned that there was a particular lack of liquidity in Russian pulp and paper stocks.
The only pulp and paper stock on the Russian Trading System is Kotlassky CBK and it last traded on October 11.

MC said Kondopoga, based in Karelia close to the Finnish border and lucrative European Union markets, had modern assets which required less capital investment than other mills. It produced high-quality newsprint which would be among the leading growth sectors of the market.
However, the free float was small so there was limited availability of stock.
Syktyvkar, whose mill in the northern Komi region is self-sufficient in energy, also produces newsprint and other products with great growth potential.
Arkhangelsk and Kotlas both required massive investment and were rated as highly speculative.

MC said Svetogorsk, 85 percent owned by Tetra-Laval, Segezhabumprom, in which Assi Doman AB has a big stake, and Volga, in which Herlitz International Trading had a stake, were solid bets. However they were illiquid due to the fact their shares were tightly held by the foreign investor.
